samples.question: What was my region's revenue by month this year?

answer.text: NZ-SOUTH revenue ranged from about $1.76m (May) to $2.21m (July) per month this year. January was $2.11m and September $1.99m. October is a partial month at $1.81m, up to 28 October.
assumptions: This year = 2026-01-01 to 2026-10-28 (year to date)
Region limited to NZ-SOUTH, the only region your role can see
Revenue is net of discounts and returns, in NZD

sql.sql:
select date_trunc('month', s.order_date)::date as period, sum(s.net_amount_nzd) as revenue
from marts.fct_sales as s
where s.order_date between %(start_date)s and %(end_date)s
group by 1
order by 1
limit %(row_limit)s

samples.question: Who are my top 5 customers by revenue last quarter?

answer.text: Your top customer last quarter was Southern Engineering Solutions Ltd at $118,428 NZD. Next were Summit Outdoor Co Ltd ($91,754), Northern Engineering Group Ltd ($89,065), Saltwater Safety Group Ltd ($87,772) and Northern Engineering Depot Ltd ($84,328).
assumptions: Revenue is net of discounts and returns, in NZD
Covers NZ-SOUTH only, which is the region your role can see

sql.sql:
select c.customer_name as customer, sum(s.net_amount_nzd) as revenue
from marts.fct_sales as s
inner join marts.dim_customer as c on c.customer_key = s.customer_key
where s.order_date between %(start_date)s and %(end_date)s
group by 1
order by 2 desc nulls last
limit %(row_limit)s

samples.question: What is the largest discount I can give without approval?

answer.text: You can give up to 15% off list price per order line without approval. Anything from 15.01% to 20% needs your regional sales manager. Above that needs the national sales manager and Commercial Finance.
assumptions: Applies per order line, across all product categories including Safety Equipment.
Volume pricing in a signed customer contract counts towards the cap, but Head Office promotional prices do not.

samples.question: How many support tickets did my customers open last month, by priority?

answer.text: Customers in NZ-SOUTH opened 181 tickets last month (September 2026). By priority: P3 had 91, P4 had 50, P2 had 29 and P1 had 11.
assumptions: Data limited to NZ-SOUTH, the region your role can see
Total of 181 is the sum of the four priority rows

sql.sql:

from marts.fct_tickets as t
where t.opened_date between %(start_date)s and %(end_date)s

samples.question: What should I focus on with tourism operators in my region?

answer.text: The NZ-SOUTH sales guide says to bundle Climbing and Safety Equipment with fitting and inspection advice for tourism operators. Their main buying peak is summer (December–February) for Camping, Hiking and Climbing, so line up bundles before then. Operators often ask for deeper discounts before summer. Stay within the 15% cap, use the Discount Approval Process, and offer volume terms instead. Stock ships from Christchurch, and Queenstown deliveries take two days.
assumptions: Read 'focus' as the policy guidance in the regional sales guide; no sales data was pulled.

samples.question: Which region had the highest revenue last quarter?

answer.text: AU-EAST had the highest revenue last quarter at about NZD 13.55 million. NZ-NORTH was next at NZD 8.81 million, then NZ-SOUTH at NZD 6.24 million and AU-WEST at NZD 5.83 million.

samples.question: Which sales reps gave the highest average discount on Safety Equipment in AU-EAST since April 2026?

answer.text: Jake Morrison gave by far the highest average discount on Safety Equipment in AU-EAST since April 2026, at 23.06%. The next highest were Ruby Singh (3.53%), Daniel Fraser (2.91%), Olivia Ngata (2.90%) and Arjun Thompson (2.89%).
assumptions: Average discount off list price on sales lines, filtered to region AU-EAST and category Safety Equipment

sql.sql:
select r.rep_name as sales_rep, round(avg(s.discount_pct) filter (where s.line_type = 'sale'), 2) as avg_discount_pct
from marts.fct_sales as s
inner join marts.dim_sales_rep as r on r.sales_rep_key = s.sales_rep_key
inner join marts.dim_product as p on p.product_key = s.product_key
where s.order_date between %(start_date)s and %(end_date)s and p.category = any(%(filter_0)s) and s.region = any(%(filter_1)s)
group by 1
order by 2 desc nulls last
limit %(row_limit)s

samples.question: What was the SLA breach rate for P1 tickets by region in January 2026?

answer.text: In January 2026, AU-WEST had by far the highest P1 SLA breach rate at 80.0%. NZ-SOUTH was next at 14.29%, then AU-EAST at 10.53% and NZ-NORTH at 5.88%.
assumptions: Breach rate = percentage of P1 tickets that breached their resolution SLA

sql.sql:
select t.region as region, round(100.0 * avg(t.is_sla_breached::int), 2) as sla_breach_rate
from marts.fct_tickets as t
where t.opened_date between %(start_date)s and %(end_date)s and t.priority = any(%(filter_0)s)
group by 1
order by 2 desc nulls last
limit %(row_limit)s

samples.question: How long do customers have to return unused products for change of mind?

answer.text: Customers have 30 days from delivery to return unused products in original packaging for a change of mind, and they receive a credit note. A 10% restocking fee applies to returns over NZD 500. Custom-cut rope, opened safety consumables and clearance items can't be returned for change of mind.

samples.question: How has gross margin % on Safety Equipment in AU-EAST changed by quarter since 2025?

answer.text: Safety Equipment gross margin in AU-EAST was steady at about 46% from Q1 2025 to Q1 2026 (45.9%, 46.3%, 46.0%, 46.0%, 46.3%). It dropped to 38.1% in Q2 2026, about 8 points lower, and has stayed near 38% since (38.1% in Q3 and 38.0% in Q4 to date). I haven't looked into the cause of the drop.
assumptions: Quarters are calendar quarters; Q4 2026 (from 2026-10-01) is partial
Region filter AU-EAST, product category Safety Equipment

sql.sql:
select date_trunc('quarter', s.order_date)::date as period, p.category as product_category, round(100 * sum(s.margin_nzd) / nullif(sum(s.net_amount_nzd), 0), 2) as gross_margin_pct
from marts.fct_sales as s
inner join marts.dim_product as p on p.product_key = s.product_key
where s.order_date between %(start_date)s and %(end_date)s and p.category = any(%(filter_0)s) and s.region = any(%(filter_1)s)
group by 1, 2
order by 1
limit %(row_limit)s

samples.question: How much is overdue in accounts receivable, by region?

answer.text: Total overdue AR is about NZD 10.17 million. AU-EAST has the most at NZD 3.58m, then NZ-NORTH at 3.08m, AU-WEST at 1.79m and NZ-SOUTH at 1.71m.
assumptions: Outstanding NZD on invoices past their due date, as at today, with no time range applied.
AUD converted to NZD at the monthly rate.
The total is the sum of the four regions.

sql.sql:
select i.region as region, round(sum(i.outstanding_nzd) filter (where i.days_overdue > 0), 2) as ar_overdue_amount
from marts.fct_invoices as i
group by 1
order by 2 desc nulls last
limit %(row_limit)s

samples.question: What are our standard credit terms, and when is an account put on hold?

answer.text: Standard terms are 30 days from invoice date, unless a signed contract says otherwise. Once an invoice is 60+ days overdue, new orders need Finance approval. An account goes on stop if any invoice is 90+ days overdue or the balance exceeds the credit limit.

samples.question: A customer says their TrailPeak tent zip split. What should I do?

answer.text: This is a confirmed supplier defect on the TrailPeak 2-Person Tent (CMP-0001). First, get the batch code from the white label inside the tent bag. samples.question: What is the escalation process for a P1 ticket?

answer.text: Within the first hour, phone the customer, assign an owner who stays on the ticket, and post it in the regional P1 channel. In hours 2 to 6, check other warehouses' stock (inter-region transfers need no manager approval) and update the customer every 2 hours. If no fix is in sight by hour 4, escalate to the regional support lead. If it won't be resolved within 8 hours, the support lead informs the regional sales manager and the customer's account owner, and agrees a recovery plan with the customer. After resolution, record the root cause category. Clusters of P1 breaches in a region are reviewed in the weekly SLA meeting.
